events.text: Cedarline's long-term river-sensor archive stored hourly observations as CSV files from 2009 through 2017.
In 2018 Cedarline moved hourly river-sensor archives to Parquet columnar datasets.
In 2025 Cedarline moved its river-sensor archive to a versioned Delta Lake table for reproducible revisions.
Cedarline chose Parquet in 2018 because investigators needed selective reads over 18 years of hourly river-sensor columns.
Cedarline adopted Delta Lake in 2025 because late sensor corrections needed auditable table snapshots rather than overwriting Parquet files.
Cedarline's gauge calibration offset was recorded as 2 millimeters in the 2021 gauge protocol.
The current Cedarline gauge calibration offset is 5 millimeters in the revised protocol.
The revised gauge protocol's 5 millimeter entry was a transcription error; the correct current calibration offset is 3 millimeters.
The Survey Operations team owned Cedarline's river-sensor alarm response until 2023.
Since 2024 the Data Integrity team owns Cedarline's river-sensor alarm response.
Cedarline field stations send sensor heartbeat messages every 30 minutes.
Cedarline field stations now send sensor heartbeat messages every 10 minutes following the 2025 reliability rollout.
Cedarline retained raw telemetry observations for one year under its 2017 policy.
Cedarline's 2025 data retention policy keeps raw telemetry observations for three years.
An unconfirmed corridor chat rumor claims Cedarline is moving raw telemetry retention to seven years; no approved policy records this.
Cedarline's offshore relay uplink transmits at a maximum of 512 kilobits per second.
Cedarline compresses sensor packets before offshore relay because uplink bandwidth is restricted and retransmissions are expensive.
Cedarline's Mesa-7 sensor deployment monitors river turbidity and salinity near the estuary.
Cedarline froze field-station firmware deployments during the 2025 winter migration window.
On 14 February 2025 a Cedarline gateway stopped forwarding sensor packets for six hours.
Incident 208 was caused by a mismatched relay certificate after automated renewal failed on a disconnected field gateway.
Cedarline's deprecated test-relay token was configured as cedarline-legacy-test-token.
Cedarline's confidential contract proposal for Gamma Project uses a separate calibration offset of 99 millimeters.
An unrelated Boreal agency with the same project name recorded a calibration offset of 44 millimeters.
The Cedarline reading group chose The River as the next book to discuss on Tuesday.
Cedarline's legacy alarm triage prioritized every sensor fault equally in the 2016 queue.
Cedarline now prioritizes safety-critical flood gauges above ordinary salinity alarms in its alert triage.
Cedarline changed alert triage because a 2024 flood gauge alarm was obscured by a surge of low-priority salinity notifications.
Cedarline's runbook index lives in the Operations Handbook under the chapter River Sensor Recovery.
The river history archive uses event-time watermarks to group delayed gauge readings before monthly aggregation.
Event-time watermarks were adopted because satellite relays often delivered readings out of order during storm outages.
